question.text: Ferdinand and his wife were assassinated by this 19-year old Yugoslav nationalist. He was a member of the Black Hand, which planned Franz Ferdinand's assassination.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.text: In this nation, the Gorbachev administration transferred power to Ion Iliescu [ill-YES-koo] after the revolt against, and public execution of, Nicolae Ceausescu [choh-SHESS-koo].
swap.clue: A ruler of this country planned to build a number of enormous domed buildings called "hunger circuses," which would have served as hubs for food distribution.

question.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
question.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
question.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Soviet bloc countries.
swap.text: Josip Broz Tito led this communist country, which, in 1992 splintered into several Balkan states, like Croatia, Serbia, and Slovenia.
swap.clue: This country's Partisans were led by a man who once sent a threatening letter to another world leader reading, "if you don't stop sending killers , I'll send one to Moscow."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Yugoslav breakup.
question.text: This last dictator of Yugoslavia and first president of Serbia and Montenegro is widely held responsible for the war crimes that took place during the Balkan Wars. He died in a prison cell in The Hague following an international tribunal.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: Marco Polo's journey is often discussed in European and world history courses, but the authority of his texts is questionable.
swap.text: Polo describes his father and uncle travelling to a namesake city to meet the Volga era of these peoples. Basil II ["the second"] was known for slaying these people during their wars with the Byzantines.
swap.answerHtml: Bulgars [accept Old Great Bulgaria, Volga Bulgaria, or First Bulgarian Empire]
swap.clue: Many members of this ethnicity were killed by bashi-bazouk (BYE-jee-buh-ZOOK) soldiers during the April Uprising in namesake "horrors."

question.leadin: In this leader's last public appearance, people shouted "Timisoara" in reference to an uprising he had violently suppressed.
question.text: Name this long-time Communist leader of Romania. This man and his wife's execution was nearly caught on live television following a 1989 revolution.
question.clue: Thousands of orphans were crammed into orphanages such as Cighid during this man's reign.

swap.leadin: This country's national hero, Skanderbeg ("SKAN-der-beg"), led the League of Lezhe ("LEH-zhuh") against the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: Name this country which was annexed by Italy during World War II. A communist dictator of this country, Enver Hoxha ("HOH-jah"), ordered the construction of thousands of bunkers.
swap.clue: This nation was flooded with refugees from the nearby Kosovo War, and joined NATO in 2009.

question.leadin: These two provinces were annexed by Austria-Hungary in 1908, despite that country having agreed to return them to the Ottoman Empire.
question.text: Identify these two provinces ruled as part of a "Condominium." These provinces were annexed at the same time that Bulgaria declared its independence.
question.clue: The Stanak assembly governed a kingdom named for this country, founded by Tvrtko I of the Kotromanic dynasty, until its 1464 conquest.

swap.text: Out With The Old Founded in the fourteenth century as Dambovita Citadel, this key city along the trade route to Constantinople became the residence of the Walachian prince. The home of the headquarters of Cominform from 1948 to 1956, much of its Old City was demolished for new buildings on a tributary of the Danube. For 15 points-name this Eastern European city.
swap.clue: A coup led by this city's orthodox Metropolitan Neophyte ended its post-1848 revolutionary period.

question.leadin: This man used a fortress at Poenari Castle.
question.text: Name this Prince of Wallachia still considered a folk hero in Romania. He is best known today for reportedly brutally executing his enemies, such as the Ottomans, by penetrating them with stakes.
question.answerHtml: Vlad the Impaler [or Vlad Tepes; or Vlad III; or Vlad Dracula]
question.clue: His younger brother Radu the Handsome spent most of his life as a hostage in Adrianople but returned to overthrow him in 1462, leading to his exile at the court of Matthias Corvinus until a later reconquest of Tirgoviste.

swap.leadin: Identify these allies of Adolf Hitler.
swap.text: This Romanian dictator, who came to power in 1940 by forcing the abdication of King Carol, established the National Legionary State, which shipped thousands of his own people to Nazi death camps. He was executed by the Communist regime.
swap.clue: He was the first non-monarch in his country to call himself the "Conducator."

question.text: The Cyrillic script, which later supplanted Glagolitic, was developed in this empire during the rule of Tsar Simeon I. Another branch of this empire formed a namesake state on the Volga river in the 9th century CE.
question.clue: From the 7th century onwards, the empire fought a series of wars with this state for control of Thrace and Greece. In the 10th century, this state reached its greatest territorial extent under Simeon I.

swap.text: This 1878 settlement of the Russo-Turkish War created several new Slavic states with autonomy from the Ottoman Empire, but it was modified at the Congress of Berlin after Bismarck found it upsetting to the balance of power.
swap.clue: This 1878 treaty, which ended the Russo-Turkish War and was softened at the Berlin Congress, recognized the independenece of Serbia, Montenegro, Romania, and Bulgaria.

question.leadin: This man defended the castle of Kruja several times.
question.text: Name this former captain who defected from the services of the Ottoman Sultan to found the League of Lezhe (LEH-zhuh). He is known by a corruption of a Turkish title which translates into English as "Lord Alexander."
question.answerHtml: George Kastrioti Skanderbeg [or Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu; or İskender Bey]
question.clue: Pope Calixtus II chose this man to be Captain General of the Holy See in 1457.

swap.leadin: During the Battle of Nis [niche], this man deserted from the forces of Murad II.
swap.text: Name this man, who was captain general of the League of Lezhe and led its forces to victory at Torvioll in 1444.
swap.clue: The Rilindja period of literary flourishment drew from that biography of this "Prince of the Epirotes" by Marin Barleti.

question.leadin: The organization headed by this man carried out a reign of terror in the 1930s that included the Velebit Uprising and it responded to King Alexander I's challenge to kill him by doing just that.
question.text: Name this leader of the Ustase movement, who used that position to persecute Jews, Serbs and Roma in concentration camps like Jasenovac.

swap.text: The hygiene practices of the lazaret were adopted from quarantine practices of this historical state that controlled much of Dalmatia until the 19th century. It was centered on the modern-day city of Dubrovnik.
swap.clue: This merchant republic centered at the port of Dubrovnik in modern-day Croatia.

question.leadin: After this man was diagnosed with polycythemia, he joked that he was "suffering from an excess of reds."
question.text: What Archbishop was controversially put on trial by Tito and convicted for treason for his relationship with the Ustase government during World War II? While eventually released from prison, he died soon after and was declared a martyr years later by Pope John Paul II.

swap.leadin: Leaders of this movement were incorrectly linked to the murder of ambassador Vladimir Rolovic in Sweden, which had been committed by one of their nation's fascist terrorist cells.
swap.text: Name this nationalistic revival movement of the late 1960s and '70s, of which Savka Dabcevic-Kucar was a major leader. Josip Tito's government arrested many of the intellectuals who signed a "Declaration on the... Language" during this movement.
swap.clue: In 1971, Yugoslavia was shaken by this "mass national movement," in which the namesake ethnic group agitated for increased autonomy, but was crushed at the village of Karadjordjevo. It did result in the promulgation of a new constitution in 1974.
